searchText: It's an elliptic curve fast linear combination So, at realistic block sizes equivalent to around ~1/10 ECMUL per 32 bytes So around 10 us per 32 bytes, or 300 ns per byte? I'm fairly out of my depth on this, working my way in, but how does that relate to the stated disadvantage in this document: https://notes.ethereum.org/@dankrad/new_sharding >Compute KZG proofs for 32 MB of data in ~1s. This requires a 32-64 core CPU. I think a machine that is capable can be built for <5,000$, proof of concept to be implemented. According to conversations with Dag Arne Osvik, it’s likely possible to do this on a GPU much cheaper Does that only become an issue when PBS/full sharding becomes a thing?
